tasks.short: Inspect, test and diagnose equipment repairs

steps.what: Read the actual work orders and schematic drawings, match them to the motor or power tool and clarify the reported problem and applicable equipment variant before inspection.
Inspect and test equipment to locate damage or worn parts, using actual physical observations and appropriate test instruments within the existing safe repair procedure.
Diagnose malfunctions and determine required repairs from the actual findings and schematic, distinguish possible causes and seek further evidence where the fault remains uncertain.

tasks.design: Retain work-order and schematic reading, physical testing and diagnosis with the repairer. Existing {DOCS} access already supplies the relevant drawing; no new automation or saving is proposed for this diagnostic work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the actual fault requires physical evidence and interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing drawing access and instruments are sufficient; no new enabler is claimed.
tasks.still_hard: Separate a visible symptom from its underlying cause.
tasks.human_edge: Relate measured behaviour to the actual equipment and repair constraints.

ambition.what: No automatic diagnosis or repair release.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the diagnostic duties.

reach.role: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment

evidence.claim: Actual inspection, testing and fault interpretation remain distinct from recording the repair findings.

assumptions: Boundary ends with actual diagnosis and required repairs. The actual repair record is split into task 11689 and is not hidden in physical inspection; service-guide retrieval is task 11695 and not counted here. Shares are illustrative.

Work-order owner supplies asset ID, reported symptoms and original schematic reference/revision. Repairer verifies them in s1 and produces actual findings in s2-s3. Missing identity or symptom detail requires direct clarification counted in s1; no free diagnosis is assumed.

Native drawing/work-order access was considered and already adequate here. After separating the actual downstream record task, no changed diagnostic step was found. No existing instrument runtime earns labour credit and no automatic test control is proposed. Zero upkeep follows no change.
research_questions: Does native access already expose the correct schematic for each work order?

already_counted.description: Actual work-order reading, physical inspection/testing and diagnosis remain in s1-s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All actual diagnostic actions retain full effort; recording is separately represented in task 11689 rather than folded into this zero-saving task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lift motors and other heavy repair units

steps.what: Check the actual unit, lifting arrangement, route and receiving position under the existing lifting procedure, resolve uncertainties and confirm the specific planned movement is ready before operating the hoist.

Lift units or parts such as motors or generators using the crane or chain hoist within the repairer's existing authorisation, carrying out the checked movement and monitoring the actual load and surrounding people throughout.

tasks.design: Retain the existing authorised physical lift and immediate readiness check. No software change, automatic crane operation or labour saving is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The movement depends on actual equipment, load and nearby people.
tasks.enabler_now: No new enabler is claimed; existing lifting arrangements remain.
tasks.still_hard: Respond immediately when the actual movement differs from the plan.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain situational awareness around the moving load.

reach.learn: Existing role boundaries and movement communication

evidence.claim: A physical lift and immediate readiness check do not disappear through record automation.

assumptions: Boundary is the statement's direct-hoist-operation alternative, performed by a repairer already authorised for it. A separate crane operator's labour is not included or claimed. Shares are illustrative.

Actual unit identity, lifting arrangement, route and destination are established from the work order and physical inspection in s1. Missing or uncertain details require clarification before the lift, counted in s1. No prepared machine command or free lift plan is assumed.

Native records and scheduling were considered but do not alter this actual movement. The statement requires no routine written lifting report, send or record commit; no administrative baseline is invented. All physical and readiness time stays. Zero change means zero upkeep.
a1 binds the specific movement checked in s1. It is the normal immediate readiness check, not an extra approval queue; changed conditions require the existing human reassessment before continuing.
research_questions: Which lifting alternative does the focal repairer actually perform?

already_counted.description: Actual readiness check and physical lift remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: No new system or upkeep is introduced.

approvals.approved_version: Specific unit, route and lifting movement checked immediately in s1

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The actual lifting work and readiness check keep full time; no record or scheduling change removes a physical action.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record required repairs, parts and labour time

steps.what: Verify actual required repairs, used parts and labour time from the repairer's observations, part labels and contemporaneous time record, resolving missing quantities or intervals without estimating them as facts.

Record repairs required, parts used and labor time in the existing maintenance work order {OTHER}; configure native asset defaults, part-catalogue selectors and explicit interval totals to reduce repeated identifiers and arithmetic while writing the actual repair description.
inputs: existing work-order asset and parts catalogue

steps.what: Check the completed repair entry against actual observations, part quantities and time intervals, including the meaning of the repair description and the distinction between required and completed work.
Commit the checked repair-record entry in the existing maintenance work-order system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native work-order fields in maintenance software {OTHER}. Reuse asset identifiers and catalogue values and total actual time intervals, while the repairer verifies facts, writes the description and checks the complete record before the separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Basic work-order entry can repeat asset details and manual interval totals.
tasks.enabler_now: Native maintenance fields can reuse explicit asset and part records.
tasks.still_hard: Recover missing time or distinguish proposed work from work actually done.
tasks.human_edge: Record an accurate account of the actual repair state.

ambition.what: No automatic invoice, warranty or release decision.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated record entry with unchanged factual accountability.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers

evidence.claim: Native maintenance fields can reuse asset identifiers, catalogue parts and actual interval totals without inventing repair facts.

assumptions: Boundary is actual repair-record preparation and commit, not physical diagnosis in 11696, repair execution or an office invoice. No other-role work is claimed or transferred. Shares are illustrative.

Repairer supplies actual diagnosis, repair state, part number/quantity and start/stop/interruption times from direct work and existing notes in s1. Existing asset master supplies ID and model. Missing facts need physical label checks or original-note recovery counted in s1; no free structured completion record is assumed.

Native selectors and defaults precede code. Saving only applies to repeated identifiers and arithmetic still done manually; already configured work orders have zero saving. Description writing, complete meaning checks and the real same-system save retain time. Consultation/access needs for staff-time records follow applicable national rules.
s3 is the ordinary check after the final entry exists, without additional self-approval activity. a1 binds the exact record, and edits invalidate it.
research_questions: Which identifiers and totals remain manually repeated in the current work order?

already_counted.description: Fact verification, retained actual entry, complete record check and commit remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain part/default mappings and test time-total exceptions.

approvals.approved_version: Final actual repair entry checked in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15.4 less 2 upkeep gives 13.4. Upper range 13 removes repeated identifiers and time arithmetic; zero where native entry is already configured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read service guides for repair information

steps.what: Find the applicable service guides and relevant sections in {DOCS}; configure native model, serial-range and revision filters with section links, checking the original guide's applicability and completeness.

Read service guides to find information needed to perform repairs, including the full relevant procedure, cautions, diagrams and variant qualifications, resolving ambiguous instructions against the original source or responsible specialist.

tasks.design: Configure native model and revision filters in {DOCS} before adding software. Reduce repeated guide navigation while the repairer still reads complete original instructions and their qualifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service-guide collections can take repeated model and section searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata and section links can narrow the original source without generating repair instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Apply the right variant and recognise an instruction that does not fit the actual equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the whole repair context rather than an isolated extracted line.

ambition.what: No generated repair procedure or automatic execution.

tasks.altitude: Less guide navigation with unchanged technical reading duties.

reach.role: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment

evidence.claim: Native document filters and section links can reduce service-guide searching without replacing original-procedure reading.

assumptions: Boundary is guide location and actual reading, not schematic diagnosis in 11696 or repair-record preparation in 11689. No routine written guide summary, send or commit is required by this task. Shares are illustrative.

Equipment label/work order supplies model, serial range and repair question; document owner supplies guide ID, revision, applicability and section references. Repairer checks them in s1. Missing metadata requires ordinary original-collection search or direct clarification counted in s1-s2, not invented applicability.

Native filters precede code. Only repeated search/navigation loses time; substantive reading and clarification remain. Existing search runtime earns no labour credit. Zero saving if guide access already works or missing metadata prevents reliable filtering.
research_questions: Can native model/revision filters reach complete relevant instructions without hiding variant cautions?

already_counted.description: Applicability verification, original guide reading and clarification remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: Maintain guide applicability metadata and section links.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 21 less 2 upkeep gives 19. Upper case removes repeated guide navigation; zero if native indexing already works or applicability cannot be verified.
